# The isoeffect inversion, scored against every randomised fractionation trial the census can read

*Generated by `scripts/trial_isoeffect_sweep.py --render-only`. The scan needs the local census; CI re-derives every figure below from the trials committed in the JSON beside this file.*

`validate_fractionation.py` checks the linear-quadratic isoeffect inversion against two trials by hand. This runs it over 294 randomised radiotherapy trials from 1,334 census shards, and asks the question two trials cannot answer: **does the inversion carry any signal, or does any pair of plausible schedules imply a plausible alpha/beta?**

## The answer

A trial reporting that its two schedules did not differ is **1.43x** more likely to have schedules that admit a positive isoeffective alpha/beta at all (65.8% of 114 arm-pairs against 45.9% of 196), 95% CI **1.16-1.78** resampling 2,000 times over trials rather than arm-pairs.

The interval EXCLUDES 1.0, so the inversion is not entailed by the arithmetic.

**Why this is the figure to lead with.** `isoeffect_alpha_beta` returns a positive value only where the dose ratio and the fraction ratio stand in a particular relation, and alpha/beta must be positive for the model to admit two arms as isoeffective at all. So this verdict needs no published band, which means it applies at every tumour site in the table including those with no alpha/beta estimate in the literature, and it imports no number from memory.

## Selection, fixed before any ratio was computed

| stage | n |
|---|--:|
| randomised trials mentioning radiotherapy | 11,062 |
| fewer than two non-boost schedules in the abstract | -10,728 |
| two or more arms | 334 |
| terminated early | -10 |
| secondary analysis by title | -30 |
| **design admissible** | **294** |
| of which report equivalence | 96 |
| of which report a difference (the control group) | 198 |

Selection is on design and reporting only. The implied alpha/beta is computed afterwards and never selects, which is what makes the control group a control.

## The confound, measured rather than assumed away

Difference-reporting trials **do** have arms further apart -- median relative dose gap 0.266 against 0.205 -- and the gap changes the geometry the positive-solution condition tests. So the enrichment could have been the gap. Stratified by it:

| relative dose gap | equivalence | difference | ratio |
|---|---|---|--:|
| [0.00, 0.15) | 20/32 = 62.5% | 25/44 = 56.8% | 1.10 |
| [0.15, 0.30) | 34/41 = 82.9% | 37/61 = 60.7% | 1.37 |
| [0.30, 0.45) | 6/14 = 42.9% | 15/45 = 33.3% | 1.29 |
| [0.45, 1.01) | 15/27 = 55.6% | 13/46 = 28.3% | 1.97 |

Stratum-pooled (Mantel-Haenszel) rate ratio **1.36** against a crude 1.43, and the enrichment holds in every stratum. The dose gap therefore accounts for little of it.

## Two exclusions that change the number, both measured

**A pair at the same fraction size carries no information, and it was 20.0% of the control group against 9.5% of the equivalence group.** If two arms share a dose per fraction `d`, the implied ratio is exactly `-d` for every such pair, so it can never admit a positive solution and asking whether it does is a question with no content. Verified across all 61 of them: none admits one. Including them raises the enrichment to 1.62x purely because the artifact is twice as common in the control group, so they are excluded from every figure above and reported here instead.

**The extractor is right in 16 of 26 hand-judged trials (61.5%), and that bounds everything here.** Judged by reading each record's own abstract against the arms returned, sampled on a named seed (`analysis/trial-isoeffect-judged.json`). It is also DIFFERENTIAL -- 68.8% on the equivalence arm against 50.0% on the control -- so the headline could in principle be an artifact of where extraction fails. Error modes:

| error mode | trials |
|---|--:|
| multi component arm | 5 |
| dose range as two arms | 2 |
| arm variants paired | 1 |
| cross trial pair | 1 |
| multi target arm | 1 |

A further 4 of 26 should have been excluded as secondary analyses and were not: the title-scoped filter misses "subset analysis", "unplanned analysis" and a modelling paper built on a trial's data.

**So the reversal is the thing to rule out, and it does not happen.** Restricted to the 16 trials whose extraction was hand-verified correct, the enrichment is **1.59x** (7/11 against 2/5) -- as large or larger than the full sweep's 1.43x, so extraction error is diluting the signal rather than creating it. Those counts are far too small to carry the result and no interval is quoted on them; what they rule out is the reversal.

## What the two groups actually are, which is weaker than their names

The label comes from the abstract's own words, and those words do not all describe the same thing. **38.5% of the equivalence group matched on DESIGN language only** -- a trial called "a randomised non-inferiority trial" is described that way whatever its result turned out to be -- while 61.5% carry language about a RESULT ("no significant difference was found", "did not differ").

| label basis | equivalence-group trials |
|---|--:|
| result only | 48 |
| both | 11 |
| design only | 37 |
| neither | 0 |

So the sweep may be separating trials whose arms were DESIGNED to be isoeffective from trials whose arms were designed to differ, rather than predicting what the trials found. Those are correlated -- a dose-finding design usually does report a difference -- but they are not the same claim, and the weaker one is the one this page can defend.

**Restricted to the equivalence trials whose abstract states a result, the enrichment is 1.37x** (39/62 against 90/196), against 1.43x on the full labelling. The verdict requires this restriction to hold as well as the hand-verified one, so a result that lived only in the design-language half would not be reported as signal.

**The classifier's own precision is NOT established, and the report will not quote one.** Hand-adjudicating the sampled trials against their abstracts, the label is confirmable by result language in only a minority, one is outright MISLABELLED (a lung trial reporting identical median survival in both arms sits in the control group because it wrote "in both groups" rather than any phrase this regex knows), and most cannot be adjudicated from an abstract at all. Those counts are in `analysis/trial-isoeffect-judged.json` under `reported_verdict`. A precision figure computed over a majority of unadjudicable rows would be a number about my reading, not about the classifier.

## What this does NOT establish

**The magnitude is a design property, not a tissue property.** A hypofractionation trial's arms are constructed EQD2-equal at an alpha/beta the designers assumed, so the inversion may recover that assumption rather than the tissue's own ratio. Nothing here measures a tissue constant. The defensible reading is that the isoeffect arithmetic tracks how trialists CONSTRUCT equivalent schedules -- weaker than measuring alpha/beta, and weaker again than predicting what a trial found, for the reason the section above gives: a large minority of the equivalence label is design language rather than a result.

**A non-inferiority result bounds a difference and does not establish equality**, so an implied ratio is an anchor and not an estimate with an interval. No figure here pools the implied values into a point estimate.

**A negative implied ratio is not an absent solution.** It is a solution the model forbids, and it is counted as such rather than dropped.

**The elapsed-time axis cannot be swept, and it is the axis START-B's failure rests on.** Per-arm treatment duration is not reliably stated in abstracts -- the curated CSV carries weeks for its two trials because a person read the papers -- so this sweep measures the enrichment and cannot test the hypothesis that overall treatment time explains the breast disagreement.

**The confound classes below are CO-MENTIONS, not arm differences.** An abstract naming chemotherapy may be describing a backbone both arms receive, so these count trials where the comparison may not be fractionation alone; they do not establish that it is not.

| class | trials |
|---|--:|
| brachytherapy component | 31 |
| chemotherapy comentioned | 72 |
| dose range in abstract | 11 |
| target volume comentioned | 42 |
| twice daily | 40 |

## The published bands, where one exists

Restricted to the 2 sites carrying a sourced band in `analysis/calibration/fractionation_trials.csv`, with that band's own source PMID. No band is typed into this generator, and a site without one gets no verdict rather than a guessed band.

| site | published band | source | equivalence in band | difference in band | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|--:|
| breast | 2.3-4.5 Gy | PMID 24055415 | 7/34 = 20.6% | 6/26 = 23.1% | 0.89 |
| prostate | 1.2-3.0 Gy | PMID 23972468 | 18/30 = 60.0% | 15/31 = 48.4% | 1.24 |

### And the per-site pattern reproduces, which is what scores P14

P14 registers that the inversion recovers a published band for one site and fails for another, on one trial each. The band table above can be read as a test of whether the SITE behaves that way across every trial the census holds, and that reading was nearly left to the reader. Derived instead:

| site | hand-read trial | implied | in band | band independent of it | sweep favours equivalence | agrees |
|---|---|--:|---|---|---|---|
| prostate | CHHiP | 2.29 Gy | yes | yes | yes (1.24x) | yes |
| breast | START-B | 0.70 Gy | no | **NO** | no (0.89x) | yes |

**2 of 2 sites agree**, and the hand-read verdicts DIFFER between them, so the agreement is not the trivial kind where every site behaved alike. The single-trial observation P14 registers therefore reflects the site and not those two trials.

**But only 1 of 2 of those bands is independent of the trial it judges.** For the other, the band's source PMID IS the trial's own paper, so the published band is an estimate the same authors made from the same data -- and the curated CSV's header claims the bands are estimated independently of these schedules, which for that row is false. It is not a useless row: a simple two-arm EQD2 inversion failing to recover what a fuller analysis of the SAME data found is a real statement about the arithmetic. It is a weaker statement than a disagreement with independent data, and this page will not let the two carry equal weight. On independent bands alone the pattern stands at 1 of 1, which is one site, and one site is an observation rather than a generalisation.

That is a statement about which band a site's trials imply, not about any tissue's alpha/beta: the arms were built to be EQD2-equal at an assumed ratio, so a site whose trials were designed around a published band will tend to imply it.

## The correctness check that licenses the rest

The extractor read these two trials' arms out of their abstracts. A person read the same two papers and wrote the schedules into the curated CSV. The implied ratios must agree.

| site | trial | hand-read | swept | delta | agrees |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| prostate | CHHiP (PMID 27339115) | 2.29 Gy | 2.29 Gy | 0.000 | yes |
| breast | START-B (PMID 24055415) | 0.70 Gy | 0.67 Gy | 0.030 | yes |

Verdict: `inversion_carries_direction_magnitude_is_design_not_tissue`.
